marks.title: Lifted gait
marks.text: She flies on her own lift with her body ahead of her pole tips. The poles push her from behind and press up on the wires, like a trolleybus's. The pose is an inverted pendulum: she holds it by trimming her angle of attack.

marks.title: She sees it
marks.text: A trolleybus on her pair of wires, braking for a stop. At this speed the gap closes at nearly seventy kilometres an hour.

marks.title: Drops out of the gait
marks.text: She stops balancing and spreads flat against the air. Her tips brake along the wire by most of what the air takes from her, so the two nearly cancel in her body and she simply falls back under her tips: the fall is her wind-up.

marks.title: Top of the back swing
marks.text: Weightless for a moment, a good metre above where she will pass the bottom, the bus's shoes a few metres ahead.

marks.title: Bottom of the drive
marks.text: Narrow, falling forward, and pulling the poles in as she passes under the tips. Angular momentum about the tips is kept, so the speed rises as the length drops.

marks.title: Release at 60°
marks.text: Both tips open in the same frame. A body on a pole moves at right angles to the pole, so poles 60° ahead of vertical launch her 60° above the horizon in the frame of the tips.

marks.title: Apex, as a hoop
marks.text: Tail curled over, both pole tips held in the fluke: a closed ring, spinning fast because it is small. The trolleybus passes underneath.

marks.title: Opened out
marks.text: The fluke lets go, the poles run out to full length and she stretches into one line. The spin collapses to a slow roll that swings the poles forward and down onto the wires.

marks.title: The catch
marks.text: One tip per wire, in the same frame. They land already running along the wire at her speed, so nothing jerks.

marks.title: Bottom of the circle
marks.text: The braking tips throw her forward and the poles go tight. She passes the bottom at roof height, ahead of the windscreen.

marks.title: Over the top
marks.text: Between the wires, narrow, poles pulled in like a gymnast's giant, just barely taut.

marks.title: The speed gain
marks.text: Her tips run hard along the wire, past her cruise speed, while she hangs behind them, narrow. Now they ease back, and that is what swings her forward: she cannot reach the lead by lift alone, because below the lead angle an open wing only drags her back.

marks.title: Catching the balance
marks.text: She arrives near the lead angle almost at rest and only now opens the wing. Lift takes her weight, the poles go from pulling to pushing, and she is balancing again.

marks.title: Back in the lifted gait
marks.text: Cruise speed, poles trailing, tips pressing up on the wires, the trolleybus far behind her. The scarf catches up last.
